name: Ephron
title: The Hittite Landowner
summary: Ephron was a Hittite, son of Zohar, who lived in Hebron. He is known for selling the cave of Machpelah and the surrounding field to Abraham as a burial place for Sarah. This transaction is one of the earliest documented property transfers in the Bible and holds great significance for Israel's connection to the land of Canaan.

keyEvents.title: Abraham's Negotiation for a Burial Place
keyEvents.description: When Sarah died, Abraham approached the Hittites in Hebron to buy a burial place. Ephron, son of Zohar, owned the cave of Machpelah that Abraham wished to purchase.

keyEvents.title: Ephron's Offer to Give the Property
keyEvents.description: Ephron first offered to give Abraham both the field and the cave for free in the hearing of the Hittites' sons, as a generous gesture.

keyEvents.title: Abraham Insists on Paying
keyEvents.description: Abraham bowed before the people of the land and insisted on paying the full price for the property, since he wanted legal ownership.

keyEvents.title: Ephron Sets the Price
keyEvents.description: Ephron stated the price at four hundred shekels of silver, a significant sum, which Abraham accepted without haggling.

keyEvents.title: The Official Property Transfer
keyEvents.description: The field of Machpelah with the cave and all the trees was formally transferred to Abraham as property, with the Hittites serving as witnesses at the city gate.

keyEvents.title: The Enduring Significance of the Burial Site
keyEvents.description: The cave of Machpelah became the burial place for several of the patriarchs and matriarchs, including Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, Jacob, and Leah, and is referenced later in the Bible.
